segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After this I heard what sounded like the loud voice of a great crowd in heaven, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Hallelujah! Salvation and glory and power belong to our God,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: for his judgments are true and just; for he has judged the great prostitute who corrupted the earth with her prostitution, and he has avenged on her the blood of his slaves.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And a second time they said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Hallelujah! Her smoke goes up forever and ever.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshipped God, who sits on the throne, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Amen! Hallelujah!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And a voice came from the throne, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Praise our God, all you his slaves, and you who fear him, the small and the great.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And I heard what sounded like the voice of a great crowd, like the sound of many waters and like the sound of mighty thunders, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Hallelujah! For the Lord God, the Almighty, has begun to reign.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Let us rejoice and be glad, and we will give him the glory, for the wedding of the Lamb has come, and his wife has made herself ready,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and it was granted to her to clothe herself in fine linen, bright and pure.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For the fine linen is the righteous acts of the holy ones.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to me,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Write: ‘Blessed are those who have been invited to the wedding banquet of the Lamb.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to me,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “These are the true words of God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And I fell down before his feet to worship him. But he said to me,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Don’t do that! I am a fellow slave with you and with your brothers and sisters who hold the testimony of Jesus. Worship God! For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And I saw heaven standing open, and look, a white horse! Its rider is called Faithful and True, and with justice he judges and makes war.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His eyes are a flame of fire, and on his head are many diadems. He has a name written that no one knows except himself,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and he is clothed in a robe dipped in blood, and his name is called the Logos of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the armies in heaven were following him on white horses, dressed in fine linen, white and pure.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: From his mouth comes a sharp sword, so that with it he may strike down the nations, and he himself will shepherd them with an iron rod; and he himself treads the winepress of the wine of the furious wrath of God the Almighty.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And on his robe and on his thigh he has a name written: King of kings and Lord of lords.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And I saw an angel standing in the sun, and he cried out with a loud voice, saying to all the birds flying high overhead,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Come, gather for the great banquet of God,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: to eat the flesh of kings and the flesh of commanders and the flesh of the mighty, the flesh of horses and of their riders, and the flesh of all, free and slave, small and great.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And I saw the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies gathered to make war against the rider on the horse and against his army.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the beast was captured, and with it the false prophet who had performed the signs in its presence, by which he deceived those who had received the mark of the beast and those who worshipped its image. The two were thrown alive into the lake of fire that burns with sulfur.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the rest were killed by the sword of the rider on the horse, the sword that came out of his mouth, and all the birds gorged themselves on their flesh.

notes.note: A Hebrew phrase meaning ‘praise Yah’ (a short form of God's name), carried over untranslated into Greek. Readers knew it from the Greek Psalms, where it stands as a heading or refrain. Its four occurrences in this chapter (verses 1, 3, 4 and 6) are the only ones in the New Testament.

This is the city called Babylon, whose fall fills chapters 17–18. The Hebrew prophets used prostitution as an image for a city's idolatry and its corrupting commerce, and the charge here is of that kind rather than literal. Older versions have ‘whore’ or ‘harlot’ and ‘fornication’; ‘prostitute’ and ‘prostitution’ keep the Greek's play on two words from one root.

The Greek word is the ordinary term for a slave, a person owned by a master, and it is the same word translated ‘slave’ in verse 18. In the Greek Old Testament ‘slaves of God’ is an honourable title for Moses and the prophets, marking them as belonging wholly to God. Most translations soften it to ‘servants’, which in modern English suggests a paid employee.

The Greek verb is in a past tense that can mark the start of a state (‘has become king’, ‘has taken up his reign’) or simply state the fact (‘reigns’). The same form opens several Psalms in the Greek Old Testament, where it is usually translated ‘the Lord reigns’. The rendering here takes it of God's rule now openly established with Babylon's fall; many translations have ‘reigns’.

notes.phrase: we will give him the glory
notes.traditional: let us give him the glory
notes.note: The manuscripts divide between ‘we will give’ and ‘let us give’, which differ in Greek by a few letters. The edition translated here prints the future; most English translations follow the other reading, which matches the two preceding verbs.

The Greek word is the ordinary one for ‘woman’ or ‘wife’, not the word for ‘bride’ used in 21:2. A betrothed woman was already called a man's wife before the wedding took place, so the word fits a wedding that has only now arrived. Many modern translations have ‘bride’.

The word is used of all members of the community as people set apart for God, echoing the Greek Old Testament's language for Israel. ‘Saints’ now suggests canonised individuals or people of exceptional virtue. Many translations keep ‘saints’; others use ‘God's people’ or ‘his holy people’.

notes.phrase: the wedding banquet of the Lamb
notes.traditional: the marriage supper of the Lamb
notes.note: The Greek word is the main meal of the day and, on formal occasions, a banquet; ‘supper’ now suggests a light evening meal. The same word returns in verse 17 for ‘the great banquet of God’, a grim counterpart in which birds feed on the fallen. That scene draws on Ezekiel 39:17–20.

The Greek can mean testimony about Jesus or the testimony that Jesus himself gave, and scholars are divided. The English ‘of’ is kept because it leaves both open. The closing sentence is correspondingly open: either witness to Jesus is the heart of prophecy, or what Jesus testified is what the prophetic Spirit speaks.

Greek has one word-family where English has two: righteous and just, righteousness and justice. Elsewhere this translation uses ‘righteousness’, but here the subject is judging and waging war, so fair judgment is meant. Most translations keep ‘in righteousness’; the phrase echoes the Psalms' picture of God judging the world.

Manuscripts vary between ‘dipped’ and several forms of ‘sprinkled’. The picture draws on Isaiah 63:1–3, where God comes with garments stained from treading the winepress. Interpreters disagree whether the blood is that of his enemies, his own, or that of the martyrs; the text does not say.

Nearly all translations have ‘the Word of God’. This translation keeps the Greek title in the four verses where it names a person, because ‘the Word of God’ now commonly means the Bible. Most scholars find the main background in the Hebrew Bible's ‘word of the Lord’ and in Wisdom traditions, which ‘Word’ reflects and ‘Logos’ does not. Wisdom of Solomon 18:15–16 pictures God's word leaping from heaven as a warrior with a sharp sword.

The verb means to tend a flock and is often used in the Greek Old Testament for a king's rule. The line quotes Psalm 2:9 in its Greek form, which has ‘shepherd’ where the traditional Hebrew text reads ‘break’. Most translations have ‘rule’; ‘shepherd’ keeps the image of a herdsman's iron-tipped club, which here is a weapon and not a gentle guide.

candidates.reason: Translators split between ‘slave’ and ‘servant’ across the whole New Testament, and the choice changes how readers hear ‘slave of God/Christ’ and the parables.
Rendered variously as fornication, sexual immorality, prostitution or unchastity; the literal and figurative uses (Gospels, Paul, Revelation) need one coordinated policy.
It ranges from bowing in homage to worship of God, and whether people ‘worship’ or ‘bow down to’ Jesus in the Gospels must be decided consistently.
The Psalm 2:9 citations (Revelation 2:27, 12:5, 19:15) and uses such as Matthew 2:6, John 21:16 and Acts 20:28 vary between ‘shepherd’, ‘tend’ and ‘rule’.
‘Supper’, ‘dinner’, ‘banquet’ and ‘feast’ all appear in translations, and the choice affects the Lord's Supper, the banquet parables and Revelation 19.

warnings: Verse 9: λόγος is not rendered with a register form (Logos) and has no register-exception note.
